goal:
Build GitPickle as an open-source, self-hosted application that independently protects authorized GitHub repositories and preserves historical Git, required LFS, and enabled wiki data in R2, S3, or B2. Support verified recovery using only archive access and required recovery keys. Provide one executable for the command-line interface, daemon, optional terminal interface, and local Model Context Protocol server. Scale to 404 repositories, support VM and container deployments, and deliver standard Git HTTPS hosting through milestone M4. Never acknowledge a committed backup or successful push that depends on the original server disk.

Owner staging decision, 15 October 2026: build and test on this machine using the GitPickle working name. Provision disposable R2 storage through the configured Cloudflare CLI and a disposable private GitHub test repository after verifying access. Use local correctness tests and small benchmarks during development. Defer live S3 and B2 tests, the real-user study, fresh-VM deployment tests, and full-size benchmarks until implementation is complete. Fresh VMs use AgentLab and the pve2 host, not pv2. Complete naming clearance as the last final-validation prerequisite. Preserve all original product requirements as final gates; deferred checks remain unverified until executed. Do not recreate early operator prerequisites or duplicate follow-ups for these deferred gates.

tasks.title: Establish a reproducible Rust development workspace
tasks.details: Create the workspace described in Appendix D with domain, application, adapters, interfaces, executable, and xtask components. Pin the toolchain and dependencies. Document Git, Git Large File Storage (LFS), and model-checking prerequisites. Implement cargo xtask check for formatting, linting, unit tests, and contract tests. A clean checkout builds and runs these checks through documented commands.

tasks.title: Define domain boundaries and user-facing contracts
tasks.details: Record architecture decisions, typed identities, context ownership, error codes, and application interfaces from sections 2–4 and Appendix A. Define versioned machine results and CLI/daemon negotiation. Create acceptance transcripts for protection, status, recovery, hosting modes, and incomplete coverage. Tests enforce dependency direction and keep provider, database, and transport types outside the domain.

tasks.title: Create deterministic fixtures and executable benchmark tooling
tasks.details: Implement seeded generators for every Appendix C fixture, including empty repositories, rewritten history, large Git/LFS data, and the 404-repository portfolio. Record measured sizes, hashes, object counts, and fixture versions. Implement the proposed bench and perf-report commands with versioned results, raw samples, environment metadata, correctness outcomes, and static reports. Measure storage requests, transferred bytes, process-tree resources, and stage durations. Invalid or incomplete runs cannot pass.

tasks.title: Provision disposable R2 and GitHub test resources
tasks.details:
User authorizes provisioning disposable Cloudflare R2 storage through the configured Cloudflare CLI and a disposable private GitHub test repository through the configured GitHub CLI. Verify account identity, access, and available capabilities before creation. Use unique test resource names and prefixes, scoped access, and ownership-checked cleanup registered before resource creation. Record nonsecret resource identifiers and the permitted test scope. Never use unrelated repositories or buckets. If the configured account lacks access, report that concrete failure. S3 and B2 accounts and live tests belong to T053/T054 at final validation; they do not block this task. No provider resources have been provisioned by this backlog update.
Owner credential handoff, 15 October 2026: use the owner-provided private bucket gitpickle-dev-tests at the documented default R2 endpoint. Runtime credentials and GITPICKLE_STORAGE_CONFIG are in /home/agent/.config/gitpickle/r2-test.env (mode 0600, outside the repository). Source that file only in the shell for authenticated operations; never print the file, secrets, or credential-bearing environment/headers. The configuration uses region auto and the gitpickle-development/ test prefix. /home/agent/.config/gitpickle/r2-access-check.json records a successful signed S3 list/write/readback/delete probe and completed object cleanup. This is access evidence, not full conformance acceptance. Treat this bucket as owner-provided persistent test infrastructure: use unique operation subprefixes, register ownership-checked cleanup for owned test objects, and never delete the bucket or unrelated objects. Cloudflare API token creation is no longer required and its earlier HTTP 403 is not a blocker. Existing GitHub CLI permission includes delete_repo. Verify/recreate only task-owned disposable GitHub fixtures where needed and preserve the resource handoff for T007. Reuse useful prior provisioning evidence from retained T004 attempts without treating cleaned-up resources as still present.

tasks.title: Implement the storage contract and provider conformance harness
tasks.details: Define typed storage operations and capability declarations. Implement deterministic storage emulation and fault injection for pagination, completed-write visibility, multipart uploads, lost responses, retries, corruption, and conditional operations. Verify content with archive digests rather than provider ETags. Separate provider retention capabilities from application append-only behavior. Tests use isolated prefixes and cannot alter existing archives.

tasks.title: Implement R2, S3, and B2 storage adapters
tasks.details:
Implement each adapter against the shared contract. Document required operations, credential permissions, endpoint configuration, retry behavior, and supported capabilities. Run deterministic adapter tests without live credentials. Keep real-provider verification explicitly separate and report unavailable capabilities rather than assuming S3 compatibility.

Owner-authorized review repair, 15 October 2026: Repair the unresolved B2 archive publication finding from review event 5178. The current B2 adapter advertises conditional_create=false, and tools/gitpickle_cloud.py rejects protection without that capability. Implement and test a provider-compatible durable publication strategy that preserves the storage and single-writer contracts. Do not enable unsupported capabilities or weaken durability guarantees. Use deterministic capability, failure, and recovery tests here; live S3/B2 acceptance remains T053/T054 and requires authorized access.

tasks.title: Verify the storage contract against R2
tasks.details: Run the existing conformance harness against the disposable R2 resources from T004. Record listing, checksums, multipart completion, ambiguous response, and conditional-publication evidence where used. Document takeover constraints and verified retention capabilities. Reject unsupported durability assumptions. Use deterministic tests for all adapters during development. Actual S3 and B2 conformance and capability evidence remain mandatory in T054 after implementation. Do not claim that R2 results establish S3 or B2 behavior.

tasks.title: Evaluate walgit and select the Git engine
tasks.details:
Run the bounded adoption spike using the specified fork at ~/walgit. Report an unavailable checkout as a prerequisite failure. Assess crate integration, licensing, dependency inventory, credentials, Git hash formats, LFS, rewritten history, snapshot portability, and the mixed portfolio. Compare against stock Git HTTP using fixed fixtures. Test crash and acknowledgment boundaries with emulated storage and the verified provider contracts. Record an adoption decision or a standard Git fallback behind a narrow GitEngine interface. Keep writable-hosting failures from blocking the backup implementation.
Owner staging: perform the adoption spike here with small fixed fixtures and verified R2 behavior. Keep deterministic contracts for all providers. Defer full-scale measurements and actual S3/B2 checks to T051/T054; those external resources do not block implementing the GitEngine boundary.

tasks.title: Model archive publication and durable job replay
tasks.details: Create ArchiveCommit.tla and JobReplay.tla before implementing their durable transitions. Model crashes, duplicate delivery, lost responses, source loss, complete dependency closure, and verification evidence. Implement cargo xtask model with pinned TLC model checker configurations. Record assumptions, specification hashes, bounds, state counts, runtime, and completion. Map actions to code boundaries and fault points. Preserve counterexamples as regression cases; timeouts remain incomplete.

tasks.title: Prototype archive recovery and finalize format version 1
tasks.details: Compare full bundles, reusable packs, and bounded incremental representations on identical fixtures. Build a restore prototype before committing the format. Specify versioned archive identity, repository identity, manifests, publication chains, evidence, and control records. Preserve refs, symbolic HEAD, Git hash algorithm, source identity, pack digests and sizes, and required LFS identifiers. Test independently traversable dependencies, empty repositories, unsupported versions, missing bases, and corrupt records. Publish independent reader documentation and measured format tradeoffs.

tasks.title: Enforce single-writer archive ownership
tasks.details: Implement a process singleton lock, per-repository mutation serialization, and durable writer identity. Open archives from another server read-only by default. Require explicit fencing and reconciliation before writable takeover. Conflicting publication chains stop mutation instead of selecting by timestamp. Tests cover competing local processes, concurrent repository jobs, conflicting chains, and unsafe takeover attempts.

tasks.title: Publish independently recoverable Git snapshots
tasks.details: Capture refs into isolated staging through native Git, validate reachable content, and upload immutable dependencies before manifests and publication records. Reconcile ambiguous writes by identity and digest. Rebuild local projections after publication and record readback verification separately. No-change captures update source evidence without Git payload uploads. Tests cover empty repositories, force-pushes, deleted refs, missing objects, lost responses, and every publication crash boundary. Keep archive deletion disabled.

tasks.title: Restore Git data without the original server
tasks.details: Implement storage inventory reconstruction and restore --from-storage without GitHub, DNS for the original server, or its database. Default to a new directory and the newest complete verified point. Support previews, explicit incomplete-point selection, and full or clearly labeled prerequisite-based bundle export. Validate archive digests, refs, HEAD, and Git integrity in clean staging. Tests remove local indexes and caches, block GitHub, and verify historical recovery and corruption detection.

tasks.title: Provide durable jobs and bounded scheduling
tasks.details: Persist acceptance and terminal records before acknowledging jobs. Reconstruct scheduling projections after SQLite loss. Scope deduplication keys to actor and operation; reject reuse with different arguments. Implement fair queues, bounded concurrency, rate limits, backoff with jitter, low-disk admission control, and safe cancellation. Tests cover duplicate requests, restart, lost acknowledgments, starvation, and concurrent jobs. Client interruption detaches without canceling server work.

tasks.title: Discover and protect authorized GitHub repositories
tasks.details: Implement authenticated pagination and stable GitHub identity mapping across renames and transfers. Support explicit repository scope and confirmed inclusion of newly authorized repositories. Schedule captures every six hours and discovery daily by default. Treat disappearing repositories as source unavailable and preserve retained history. Distinguish protect, backup, and sync semantics. Deterministic tests cover partial authorization, rate limits, credential loss, identity changes, and 404 repositories.

tasks.title: Capture and recover required LFS and enabled wiki data
tasks.details: Discover and validate required LFS content and capture enabled wiki repositories as separate coverage components. Retain Git-only progress when required content is unavailable without reporting complete verification. Restore and verify component digests independently. Tests cover missing LFS content, later availability, unavailable wikis, and unchanged captures with zero Git/LFS payload uploads. Preserve submodule pointers without fetching arbitrary dependent URLs.

tasks.title: Calculate truthful status and recovery evidence
tasks.details: Track source observation, content change, capture completion, verification, and restore-test timestamps with explicit scopes. Compute current-and-verified status from matching required coverage and freshness, with an eight-hour warning default. Keep sampled restore evidence limited to sampled repositories. Implement status, status --check, and doctor outcomes with stable errors and next actions. Test stale sources, unchanged snapshots, missing LFS, successful queries with degraded protection, and excluded GitHub metadata.

tasks.title: Model and enforce authorized execution plans
tasks.details: Create and check PlanApproval.tla before implementing plan application. Bind approvals to actor, repository IDs, destination, visibility, expected versions, digest, expiry, and impact limits. Enforce grants in application services and revalidate before execution. Tests deny changed, expired, replayed, or unauthorized plans, including a model-supplied approval boolean. Record redacted audit events and constrain agent restore destinations.

tasks.title: Secure the daemon and shared application interfaces
tasks.details: Implement authenticated management access with local binding by default and repository-scoped grants. Run unprivileged with private state paths. Reject archive traversal and unsafe destinations, sanitize Git configuration, disable repository hooks, and bound child processes. Constrain source schemes and unexpected internal-network fetching. Keep credentials out of durable policies, process arguments, logs, and responses. Security tests cover unauthorized access, malicious repository data, path attacks, and secret redaction.

tasks.title: Deliver the guided command-line workflow
tasks.details:
Implement protect github, checkout-based protect, status, backup, sync, restore, doctor, and two help levels through shared services. Resume setup without duplicate jobs or repeated completed authorization. Preview scope and changes; probe authentication, storage, capabilities, and staging disk before applying. Require separate permission for bucket creation. Preserve local remotes and uncommitted work. Support masked secrets, keyboard use, NO_COLOR, narrow output, explicit time zones, versioned JSON, and stderr diagnostics. Noninteractive calls never prompt. Test scope changes, --all, durable job IDs, --wait, and client detachment.

Owner-authorized review repair, 15 October 2026: Repair the unresolved guided first-run finding from review event 5179. tools/gitpickle_setup.py currently tells users to create policy.json and runtime.env manually. Complete guided configuration for first-run protection under gitpickle.md section 8, including preview, explicit authorization, secret handling, validation, safe resumption, and noninteractive behavior. Test that users can complete supported setup without hand-editing configuration files. Preserve existing configuration and require authorization for external changes.

tasks.title: Provide recovery cards and compatibility checks
tasks.details: Generate a nonsecret recovery card with archive identity, provider, bucket/prefix, format version, software retrieval instructions, and key-location guidance. Document independent software retention and recovery limits. Test archive-reader compatibility and CLI/daemon version negotiation. Ensure fresh recovery requires only storage access and any explicitly configured recovery keys. Do not enable optional client-side encryption without a separately tested key-recovery design.

tasks.title: Verify local and R2 portfolio recovery
tasks.details: Execute the M1 and M2 acceptance scenarios on this machine using isolated local and disposable R2/GitHub resources. Protect a private test repository, destroy only test daemon state, block GitHub access for the test process, and restore from storage. Repeat with Git/LFS/wiki coverage and small deterministic portfolio fixtures. Verify source deletion, force-push history, missing LFS, upload crashes, durable job reconstruction, and scheduling fairness. Record R2 capture, no-change, restore, and index-rebuild evidence. Equivalent live S3/B2 scenarios remain required in T054. Full-size portfolio and performance measurements belong to T051. Do not alter unrelated workloads or claim deferred tests have passed.

tasks.title: Serve authenticated read-only Git HTTPS
tasks.details: Integrate the selected Git engine behind GitEngine. Serve only committed generations and durable LFS data. Keep hosting disabled until explicitly enabled. Enforce repository authorization and reject pushes to protected mirrors with a clear explanation. Display the canonical remote URL and mode. Test ordinary clone, fetch, pull, tags, authentication failures, empty repositories, and advertised protocol features. Publish a compatibility matrix without unsupported claims.

tasks.title: Expose constrained local agent tools
tasks.details: Implement gitpickle mcp as a local stdio Model Context Protocol server with the seven tools specified in section 3. Reuse application authorization and approval rules. Return bounded, paginated results with timestamps, scope, evidence, stable IDs, and next actions. Keep protocol output free of terminal prose. Generated client configuration references a profile and preserves existing settings. Scripted tests verify idempotency, resumable jobs, unapproved-plan denial, redaction, and coverage questions answered in at most two calls.

tasks.title: Provide the optional terminal interface
tasks.details: Implement gitpickle tui with portfolio search, filters, repository details, recovery points, jobs, and reviewed operations. Reuse application services and authorization. Display backup coverage and hosting mode separately. Support keyboard navigation, small terminals, and NO_COLOR. Keep every operation available through the plain CLI and never start the interface for JSON or agent automation. Test navigation and measure startup, search latency, and resource use over 404 repositories.

tasks.title: Package reproducible VM and container deployments
tasks.details: Provide versioned binaries, systemd units, and pinned Open Container Initiative images with gitpickle serve as entrypoint. Disclose native Git dependencies and licenses. Generate a software bill of materials and artifact verification instructions. Containers run unprivileged, expose health/readiness, log to standard streams, and handle SIGTERM safely. Supply Coolify and standalone container recipes with runtime secrets. Test install, restart, upgrade, and loss of local volumes without losing committed archive data.

tasks.title: Guide remote installation and private HTTPS configuration
tasks.details: Extend setup for local execution, a Linux server over Secure Shell, and guided Coolify deployment. Verify server identity and preview installation, privileges, dependencies, and configuration changes. Detect existing Tailscale and guide private HTTPS without automatic account enrollment or public Funnel. Bind private container ports to host loopback. Document optional public reverse-proxy settings for streamed Git/LFS traffic and protected management routes. Test resumable setup and configuration isolation.

tasks.details: Use this machine for development tests and small benchmarks. Inspect and record available tools, hardware, free disk, and test isolation. Allocate only temporary project-owned directories, local process endpoints, and uniquely identified test containers when available. Preserve unrelated workloads and register ownership-checked cleanup. Avoid full-size fixture generation and heavy benchmarks on this machine. Fresh-VM provisioning, private HTTPS/Tailscale and Coolify profiles, independent evidence storage, and a pinned full-size runner remain in T055/T051 after implementation. Missing fresh-VM resources do not block local development tooling.

tasks.title: Verify deployment and Git recovery locally
tasks.details: Exercise locally available binary, daemon, and isolated container deployment paths on this machine with pinned artifacts. Verify ordinary Git clone/fetch, repository authorization, restart, deletion of test cache/index state, and recovery from R2. Record local startup and cold/warm access measurements with their limitations. Prepare reproducible systemd, Coolify, private HTTPS, and tailnet test procedures and fixtures. Live fresh-machine validation of every required deployment profile remains mandatory in T055; unavailable external hosts do not block this local task. Do not claim unrun systemd, Coolify, private HTTPS, or tailnet scenarios have passed.

tasks.details:
Wire pull-request, nightly, and release suites from Appendix C into locally runnable tooling and continuous integration. Implement the proposed fault-test command and preserve regression traces. Compare clean baseline and candidate runs against both merge base and pinned release baseline. Characterize noise before enforcing numeric timing budgets. Implement warning, confirmation, waiver, and invalid-run rules. Nightly suites include large fixtures and separately credentialed provider canaries. Archive raw evidence outside the source repository.
Owner staging: implement every suite and gate now. Validate correctness, model/fault handling, and small benchmarks on this machine. Full-size runs execute only in T051 on the final pve2 VM profile. Actual S3/B2 canaries and remote deployment acceptance remain deferred to T054/T055. Keep those gates explicitly pending; do not require their resources merely to implement and test the tooling locally.

tasks.details:

Measure unaided setup, incomplete-backup recognition, safe restore, and understanding of configured, verified, and fresh. Prepare evidence templates without presenting proposed results as observations.
Owner staging: prepare this study only during final validation, after T052. This task does not block implementation or local release-document preparation.

Failed criteria remain unresolved evidence for the release gate.

Use the specified jar and mascot direction without weakening operational wording. Complete storage/protocol, model-aware, and security reviews of the implemented product. Include available local/R2 measurements and label missing evidence. Describe M3 hosting as read-only and mark later connectors and optional capabilities unavailable. Track real-user findings, the final cleared-name application, full-size measured baseline, clean-machine recovery, and all remaining section 8 evidence in T056. Preparing documentation does not declare M3 or the public release complete. T032 and T033 are final gates, not prerequisites for writing this documentation.

tasks.title: Model durable Git publication and prove the integration boundary
tasks.details: Create GitPublish.tla before implementing writable publication. Model staged generations, object durability, publication, final acknowledgment, crash recovery, and retry ambiguity. Prototype the engine response gate against native Git semantics, including atomic and mixed-result pushes. Demonstrate that progress can stream while final success waits for durable publication. Document failures and the tested coordinator approach; keep read-only hosting available while this gate remains unresolved.

tasks.title: Implement explicit hosted mode and durable pushes
tasks.details: Add authorized hosted-repository creation and mirror conversion with a retained checkpoint and paused source updates. Require explicit reconciliation before resuming mirroring. Stage pushes privately under repository serialization, persist the resulting object closure and generation, then expose refs and acknowledge success. Reconcile committed operations after lost responses. Make LFS upload success durable and define the missing-LFS push policy. Tests prove mirroring cannot overwrite hosted refs and storage failure cannot produce local-only success.

tasks.title: Verify and document the complete M4 Git contract
tasks.details: Run standard-client tests for clone, fetch, pull, normal pushes, force-with-lease, deletions, annotated tags, multiple refs, atomic pushes, and LFS. Cover empty repositories, unusual valid names, large ref sets, and authentication failures. Publish explicit support for protocol versions, hash formats, shallow/filtered clones, signed push certificates, LFS locking, and hooks. Inject server loss at every push boundary on each supported provider and restore every acknowledged update. Report contention, durability latency, resource use, and recovery evidence. Complete technical M4 acceptance after the final S3/B2 and deployment checks. Full M3/M4 release completion, study evidence, and the last naming decision remain gated by T056. Keep retention cleanup, replication, metadata connectors, and remote agent transport deferred behind their separate future gates.
